chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Rifa'ah ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who fainted (or lost consciousness), so he said: 'The pebbles are thrown on his behalf.'

key_terms.اَلْجِمَارُ: The Jamarat (the pillars/stones at Mina where pebbles are thrown during Hajj)
key_terms.يُرْمَى: Is thrown (passive verb referring to the ritual pebbles)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who faints during the stoning of the Jamarat?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of Rami al-Jamarat is excused for one who loses consciousness, with the ritual fulfilled by proxy (*bi-al-ghayr*). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *rukhas* (dispensations) in Hajj, ensuring that physical incapacity does not invalidate the pillar, while maintaining the continuity of the ritual through a representative. It highlights the practical flexibility embedded in Shia fiqh to accommodate pilgrims' varying states of health during the intense rites of Mina.
